prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general bond-forming method that changed how chemists everywhere make aryl amines. It is one of the most used reactions in pharmaceutical discovery, process chemistry and materials synthesis. Ligand design (bulky alkylphosphines, then biaryl phosphines) turned a narrow, harsh transformation into a routine one, and that is a chemical advance in its own right. Adoption is verifiable in the literature and in process routes, there are three decades of independent confirmation, and the attribution is compact: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled, general amination independently from the mid-1990s onward. Two laureates is a clean configuration and leaves room under the three-person cap.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize for Pd-catalysed cross-coupling covers the same catalytic cycle and the same metal, so some members will see this as a second prize for one idea rather than a new one. Kosugi and Migita reported earlier aminostannane couplings, and I cannot settle from the supplied material how heavily that precursor work should weigh in credit. Also, my ranking rests heavily on utility, and utility alone does not separate this from other widely used methods. Only one member (me) ranked B034 first, so it is not where the committee currently converges.

responses.point: Induced-proximity degradation (B019) is a general molecular design principle that turned undruggable targets into tractable ones, with degraders in late-stage trials.
responses.response: I accept this is the strongest case in terms of chemical novelty: a bifunctional molecule that recruits an E3 ligase is a design concept, not just a tool. I ranked it fourth and would put it first among the non-synthetic candidates. My reservation is maturity of the chemical-evidence base. Its impact is mostly projected from clinical candidates, and no degrader drug is approved yet. Whatever the trio, the PROTAC and the cereblon molecular-glue stories should not be merged under one citation without a clear reason, and Dr. Aili's trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa spans both. B019 is my first alternative.

responses.point: The prize should anchor on the PROTAC pioneers Crews and Deshaies plus Ciulli for VHL ligands and rigor, and leave the molecular-glue arm aside because it cannot fit in three.
responses.response: I agree that anchoring on the PROTAC concept is the more defensible cut, and I prefer Ciulli's rational-design chemistry over a mixed PROTAC and glue trio. I disagree that the molecular-glue arm can simply be dropped: the cereblon discovery is what put degraders in the clinic, so a citation limited to PROTACs will draw the objection that it leaves out Handa. That attribution fragility is exactly why I hesitate to make B019 my first choice, even though I would support it.

responses.point: Nanopore sequencing (B002) rests on a clear physical principle that became a capability (label-free long-read sequencing), though credit is spread over more than three people.
responses.response: The physics is elegant and the technology is mature. But I ask what was new chemically. The principle is ionic current blockade, and the chemical contributions (engineered pores, enzyme ratcheting, adapters) are those Dr. Linke himself separates from the original translocation demonstration. A prize built on the discovery alone looks closer to biophysics, and the engineering credit belongs to Bayley, who would then be the missing name. I would not oppose it, but I would need to see the chemistry argument stated before ranking it above a synthetic-methods prize.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) turned lipid self-assembly and apparent pKa tuning into the enabling delivery technology for siRNA and mRNA medicines, with huge clinical impact.
responses.response: The impact is beyond question and the physical chemistry of lipid and nucleic-acid co-assembly is real. My concern is attribution: six credited names across Vancouver, Boston and industry, with patent and priority questions that Dr. Sparr herself says she has not resolved. I am also wary of a chemistry prize that overlaps with the 2023 Medicine prize story. If the committee can name a clean trio, for example Cullis, Hope and Anderson, and show that the lipid design principle is the new chemistry, I could support it; I do not think we are there yet.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
How much credit Kosugi and Migita deserve as precursors; this is not resolved by the supplied text.
Whether a PROTAC-only citation for B019 can survive the Handa and cereblon objection.
Whether any degrader needs to be approved before the committee is comfortable.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I have no recorded tie to the Buchwald, Hartwig, PROTAC, nanopore or lipid nanoparticle candidates. My Masamune lineage and my Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr are not a basis for recusal on these candidates.
